_note: v2 hook overrides for la Maison familiale (B05_maison). Every hook describes what is actually painted (nothing is written in the paintings); plaque words are shown only as a small blank plaque.

fr_couloir_noun.hook: Two children fight a "COOL WAR" ("koo-LWAHR") with pillows down the CORRIDOR, feathers flying.
fr_couloir_noun.why: Reworded to match the painting: the painted children have a pillow fight (no water pistols, so nothing weapon-like).

fr_immeuble_noun.hook: Across the courtyard a BLOCK OF FLATS with rows of round windows stands IMMOBILE ("ee-MUHBL").
fr_immeuble_noun.why: Reworded to match the painting: the window looks out on a real block of flats, not a model on a table.

fr_appartement_noun.hook: From the top of the block A PARTY MAN in a paper crown throws streamers out of his FLAT ("ah-pahr-tuh-MAHN").
fr_appartement_noun.why: Reworded to match the painting: the party man leans out of the top of the block of flats across the courtyard.

fr_toit_noun.hook: A TOY ("TWAH") train runs along the ROOF of the block of flats.
fr_toit_noun.why: Reworded to match the painting: the train runs on the real block's roof, not a model.

fr_lampe_noun.hook: Like English 'lamp', said LAHNP with a nasal: a girl in a blue dress switches on the reading LAMP while her tabby cat dozes on the rug nearby.
fr_lampe_noun.why: Reworded to match the painting: the girl wears a blue dress and the tabby sleeps on the rug.

fr_ampoule_noun.hook: A bare glowing LIGHT BULB hangs over the goldfish bowl, lighting up the fish's little POOL ("ahn-POUL").
fr_ampoule_noun.why: Respelling reworded so no syllable reads as pee/poo; the painting is unchanged.

fr_placard_noun.hook: Not a protest placard: placard ("plah-KAHR") is the CUPBOARD a boy peeks out of, high on the oak sideboard.
fr_placard_noun.why: Reworded to match the painting: no blank placard is painted; the boy peeks out of the cupboard.

fr_buffet_noun.hook: Like English 'buffet', said bew-FEH: a child in a white sheet pops out beside the oak SIDEBOARD going "BOO!".
fr_buffet_noun.why: Reworded to match the painting: there is no little brother beside the ghost.

fr_tapis_noun.hook: A tapir ("tah-PIH") sits proudly in the middle of the patterned RUG as if it owned it.
fr_tapis_noun.why: Respelling reworded so no syllable reads as pee/poo; the painting is unchanged.

fr_crotte_noun.hook: Text plaque only: no droppings are painted; the small blank tag hanging on the dog basket stands for DROPPING ("KROT"), the thing a good dog owner always picks up.
ex: Attention, il y a une crotte de chien sur le trottoir !
Watch out, there's a dog dropping on the pavement!
fr_crotte_noun.why: Museum plaque word: nothing is depicted; the painting shows only a small blank plaque, so the hook describes the plaque. The plaque is now a blank tag on the basket. Example gloss reworded to avoid a blocked word.

fr_chien_noun.hook: A shaggy gray DOG ("SHYAN") has dropped a red ball and waits, tongue out, for someone to throw it.
fr_chien_noun.why: Reworded to match the painting: no boy is painted beside the dog.

fr_fille_noun.hook: A GIRL with pigtails pays her FEE ("FEEY") at a little cardboard-box booth.
fr_fille_noun.why: Reworded to match the painting: the booth is made of cardboard boxes. Text pass 2026-10-28 (hook lint): respelling (FEE) -> (FEEY) to match the card.

fr_cousin_noun.hook: A pigeon COOs ("koo-ZAN") on the lap of the boy COUSIN sitting in his little tent.
fr_cousin_noun.why: Reworded to match the painting: the pigeon sits on the cousin's lap; there is no photo frame.

fr_tante_noun.hook: The AUNT, still a girl at heart, knits woolly socks inside the spotted pink TENT ("TAHNT").
fr_tante_noun.why: Reworded to match the painting: the tent is spotted, not striped.

fr_familial_adj.hook: The FAMILY dog wears the tartan family scarf in its oval portrait: everything here is FAMILIAL ("fah-mee-LYAHL").
fr_familial_adj.why: Reworded to match the painting: the dog's scarf is tartan, not striped. Text pass 2026-10-28: bracketed respelling matched to the card (fah-mee-LYAL -> fah-mee-LYAHL).

fr_epoux_noun.hook: A bride and her SPOUSE sit side by side on a church bench, A PEW ("ay-POU").
fr_epoux_noun.why: Respelling reworded so no syllable reads as pee/poo; the couple sit on a bench.

fr_parent_noun.hook: A PARENT in red pushes the family pram with a green PARROT ("pah-RAHN") riding on her shoulder.
fr_parent_noun.why: Reworded to match the painting: the painted parent is a woman.

fr_gendre_noun.hook: The new SON-IN-LAW sits with a big white GANDER ("ZHAHNDR") tucked under his arm.
fr_gendre_noun.why: Reworded to match the painting: there is no bay window in the photo.

fr_papi_noun.hook: GRANDPA in his green armchair hugs a floppy-eared PUPPY ("pah-PIH") on his lap.
fr_papi_noun.why: Respelling reworded so no syllable reads as pee/poo; the photo has no fire.

fr_cuisine_noun.hook: A young QUEEN ("kwee-ZEEN") in a gold crown and white apron rules her KITCHEN, waving a wooden spoon.
fr_cuisine_noun.why: Reworded to match the painting: the queen waves the spoon; she is not stirring.

fr_vitre_noun.hook: A girl draws on the glassy (vitreous, "VEETR") WINDOW PANE of the kitchen window.
fr_vitre_noun.why: Reworded to match the painting: it is the kitchen window, not a laundry door.

fr_boite_noun.hook: A little wooden toy BOAT ("BWAHT") with a white sail sits in an open cardboard BOX.
fr_boite_noun.why: boat ~ boîte; the boat is inside the box

fr_four_noun.hook: A cook in a chef's hat waves FOUR ("FOOR") fingers by the brick OVEN.
fr_four_noun.why: Reworded to match the painting: the cook waves by the oven.

fr_cendrier_noun.hook: Text plaque only: no ashtray is painted anywhere in the house; the blank cream plaque on the kitchen wall stands for the word ASHTRAY ("sahn-dree-YAY").
fr_cendrier_noun.why: Museum plaque word: nothing is depicted; the painting shows only a small blank plaque, so the hook describes the plaque.

fr_couteau_noun.hook: A dove COOs on the KNIFE, perched on its TOE: koo-TOH = coo + toe.
fr_couteau_noun.why: Reworded to match the painting: the knife lies in the drawer; there is no cutting board.

fr_plaque_noun.hook: A boy polishes the round brass PLATE on the wardrobe: "PLACK, PLACK!" goes his cloth.
fr_plaque_noun.why: Reworded to match the painting: the boy is not dressed as a knight.

fr_lit_noun.hook: Little LEE ("LEE") sits up in the big wooden BED with her knitting.
fr_lit_noun.why: Reworded to match the painting: the painted knitter is a little girl, not a granny.

fr_reveur_adj.hook: A DREAMY girl in the middle of the dream cloud rests her chin on her hands and gazes up ("reh-VUHR").
fr_reveur_adj.why: Reworded to match the painting: the girl is inside the dream cloud.

fr_baillement_noun.hook: A teddy bear waves "BYE!" mid-YAWN ("bah-yuh-MAHN"), mouth wide open.
fr_baillement_noun.why: Reworded to match the painting: the yawner is a teddy bear (stripes are kept for Monsieur Verbe).

fr_eveil_noun.hook: In the framed picture a bride in A VEIL ("ay-VEHY") greets the sunrise, wide AWAKE.
fr_eveil_noun.why: Reworded to match the painting: the bride wears the veil at sunrise. Gloss simplified.

fr_rappel_noun.hook: A tiny toy drummer in a little frame on the wall RAPS ("rah-PEHL") out a REMINDER.
fr_rappel_noun.why: Reworded to match the painting: the drummer is in a small frame, not on a cork board.

fr_pantalon_noun.hook: Twist on 'pantaloons': a clown dances in giant polka-dot TROUSERS ("pahn-tah-LOHN").
fr_pantalon_noun.why: Reworded to match the painting: the trousers are polka-dot (stripes are kept for Monsieur Verbe).

fr_dentelle_noun.hook: A white LACE veil DANGLES ("dahn-TEHL") from its hanger in the wardrobe, its scalloped edge swaying.
fr_dentelle_noun.why: dangle ~ dentelle; the lace itself dangles

fr_blouson_noun.hook: A puffy BLUE ("BLOO") bomber JACKET, a blouson, hangs in the wardrobe.
fr_blouson_noun.why: Reworded to match the painting: the jacket hangs in the wardrobe; no boy is painted.

fr_cravate_noun.hook: A CRAB sits in a wooden VAT ("krah-VAHT") of water wearing a polka-dot TIE.
fr_cravate_noun.why: Reworded to match the painting: the tie is polka-dot.

fr_culotte_noun.hook: Text plaque only: no underwear is painted; the small blank plaque on the wall above the chest of drawers stands for KNICKERS, "a CUTE LOT" ("kew-LOT").
fr_culotte_noun.why: Museum plaque word: nothing is depicted; the painting shows only a small blank plaque, so the hook describes the plaque.

fr_semelle_noun.hook: A shoe pokes out of the bottom drawer, its muddy SOLE showing: "SMELL ("suh-MEHL") that!"
fr_semelle_noun.why: Reworded to match the painting: the shoe sticks out of the drawer; no boy is painted.

fr_echarpe_noun.hook: A long red SCARF spills out of the top drawer, its fringe as SHARP ("ay-SHAHRP") as a row of teeth.
fr_echarpe_noun.why: Reworded to match the painting: no shark is painted; only the scarf.

fr_fragment_noun.hook: The FRAGMENTS of a broken blue-and-white vase lie scattered on top of the chest: "Frag, MAN!" ("frahg-MAHN").
fr_fragment_noun.why: Reworded to match the painting: the pieces lie on the chest; no boy is painted.

fr_smoking_noun.hook: False friend: a black TUXEDO ("smo-KEENG") with a bow tie hangs on the clothes rail. In French, this word only ever means the dinner jacket.
fr_smoking_noun.why: Reworded to match the painting: the tuxedo hangs on the rail.

fr_manche_noun_f.hook: La manche: the long SLEEVE of a blue shirt dangles over the shelf edge, just right to MUNCH ("MAHNSH").
fr_manche_noun_f.why: Reworded to match the painting: no cat is painted; only the sleeve.

fr_habit_noun.hook: A little dressmaker's dummy on the shelf wears a whole OUTFIT, tailcoat and bow tie, as neat as A BEE ("ah-BEE").
fr_habit_noun.why: Reworded to match the painting: the outfit is on a dummy; no bee is painted.

fr_crepe_noun_m.hook: Le crêpe is the FABRIC, not the pancake: a crinkly dark CREPE ("KREHP") cloth lies folded on the bottom shelf.
fr_crepe_noun_m.why: Reworded to match the painting: the cloth lies on the shelf; no pancake is painted.

fr_toilette_noun.hook: A white poodle grooms the bulldog's ear beside the bath: "TWO, LET me finish!" ("twah-LEHT"), she is doing his TOILETTE (grooming, not the WC).
fr_toilette_noun.why: Reworded to match the painting: the poodle grooms the bulldog in the tub.

fr_tabouret_noun.hook: A ginger TABBY cat ("tah-boo-REH") sits up on the wooden STOOL.
fr_tabouret_noun.why: Reworded to match the painting: the cat is a ginger tabby.

fr_mouchoir_noun.hook: A little brown calf holds a lace HANDKERCHIEF in her mouth: "MOO" ("moo-SHWAHR").
fr_mouchoir_noun.why: Reworded to match the painting: the calf is brown.

fr_pipe_noun.hook: Text plaque only: no pipe is painted anywhere in the house; the small blank plaque on the laundry wall stands for the word PIPE ("PIHP").
ex: La vieille pipe en bois est rangée dans la vitrine du musée.
The old wooden pipe is kept in the museum display case.
fr_pipe_noun.why: Museum plaque word: nothing is depicted; the painting shows only a small blank plaque, so the hook describes the plaque. Example replaced: the v1 example describes smoking.

fr_chose_noun_f.hook: La chose: a wicker hamper of THINGS for school SHOWS ("SHOHZ"): an umbrella, hats, a rubber duck, a wig.
fr_chose_noun_f.why: Reworded to match the painting: the hamper holds an umbrella (no swords).

fr_coffre_noun.hook: Twist on 'coffer': a boy opens a dusty CHEST and covers his mouth as he COUGHS ("KOFR") in the golden dust.
fr_coffre_noun.why: Reworded to match the painting: golden dust motes rise from the chest.

fr_grenier_noun.hook: Twist on 'granary': a black cat sits on sacks of grain under the eaves of the ATTIC.
fr_grenier_noun.why: Reworded to match the painting: the cat is black.

fr_sous_sol_noun.hook: Up the stairwell from the cellar a SOUS-chef carries a flat SOLE fish ("soo-SOL") from the BASEMENT.
fr_sous_sol_noun.why: Reworded to match the painting: the stairwell is at the bottom right, not the far left.

fr_colocataire_noun.hook: Two laughing boys, FLATMATES, tug at the same giant brass LOCK key ("koh-LOK"), nearly in TEARS ("TEHR") of laughter.
fr_colocataire_noun.why: Reworded to match the painting: two boys tug the key.

fr_fondement_noun.hook: A little boy in a yellow hard hat, a very FOND little MAN ("fohnd-MAHN"), hugs the big stone FOUNDATION pillar.
fr_fondement_noun.why: Reworded to match the painting: the builder is a little boy and the stone is a pillar.

fr_maconnerie_noun.hook: Grandma ("MA") in her apron lays bricks into a low wall, SO neat ("mah-so-nuh-REE"): MASONRY.
fr_maconnerie_noun.why: Reworded to match the painting: she builds a low wall, not an arch. Text pass 2026-10-28: bracketed respelling matched to the card (mah-SO-nuh-REE -> mah-so-nuh-REE).

fr_hebergement_noun.hook: A brown BEAR ("BEHR") in a red nightcap sits up in a wooden guest bed: ACCOMMODATION.
fr_hebergement_noun.why: Reworded to match the painting: the nightcap is plain red (stripes are kept for Monsieur Verbe) and the bed is wooden.

fr_vestibule_noun.hook: A man in a waistcoat, a VEST, leads a big BULL ("BEWL") past the open door of a VESTIBULE across the street.
fr_vestibule_noun.why: Reworded to match the painting: seen through the skylight; no rug is painted.

fr_marelle_noun.hook: A red-capped mushroom (think MOREL, "mah-REHL") hops along the chalk HOPSCOTCH squares.
fr_marelle_noun.why: Reworded to match the painting: the painted mushroom is a red cap.

fr_billard_noun.hook: A boy lines up his shot at the POOL TABLE and a big fuzzy BEE lands right at the tip of his cue: "BEE, YARD!" ("bee-YAHR").
fr_billard_noun.why: bee + yard ~ billard; the bee sits on the cue at the table

fr_poupee_noun.hook: A girl hugs her floppy rag DOLL, really a PUPPET ("pou-PAY").
fr_poupee_noun.why: Respelling reworded so no syllable reads as pee/poo; the painting is unchanged.

fr_ping_pong_noun.hook: A boy whacks the ball across the PING-PONG table: "PING! PONG!"
fr_ping_pong_noun.why: Respelling reworded so no syllable reads as pee/poo; the painting is unchanged.

fr_pelote_noun.hook: A fluffy white BALL of wool sits at the cat's feet, round as a PILOT's ("puh-LOT") helmet.
fr_pelote_noun.why: Reworded to match the painting: no kitten is painted; the ball of wool lies in the chest.

fr_enigme_noun.hook: A sphinx-like gray cat sits in the open toy chest and stares at you, posing a RIDDLE ("ay-NEEGM").
fr_enigme_noun.why: Reworded to match the painting: the cat sits without raising a paw.

fr_haie_noun.hook: A horse leaps toward a round stack of HAY ("EH") in front of the tall HEDGE.
fr_haie_noun.why: Reworded to match the painting: the horse leaps toward the hay in front of the hedge.

fr_pelouse_noun.hook: A green ball, like a giant PEA, rolls LOOSE ("puh-LOOZ") across the LAWN.
fr_pelouse_noun.why: Reworded to match the painting: a green ball rolls across a plain lawn.

fr_gazon_noun.hook: A boy has put the GAS ON ("gah-ZOHN"): his red jerry can stands by the mower as he mows the TURF.
fr_gazon_noun.why: Reworded to match the painting: the mower is pushed by a boy.

fr_square_noun.hook: A stone fountain ringed by a clipped box hedge: a little public GARDEN ("SKWAHR") in miniature.
fr_square_noun.why: Reworded to match the painting: the hedge rings a fountain.

fr_serrure_noun.hook: The green door's LOCK plate is a brass lion's head that goes "ROAR!" ("say-REWR") when you turn the key.
fr_serrure_noun.why: Reworded to match the painting: the lion's-head lock plate is on the door.

fr_maman_noun.hook: In one little portrait a MAMA duck leads her line of four ducklings: MOM ("mah-MAHN").
fr_maman_noun.why: Reworded to match the painting: the duck family is in a portrait, not on a rug.

fr_promesse_noun.hook: Two little hands link little fingers on the bedside table: a PROMISE never to MESS ("proh-MEHS") up the bed again.
fr_promesse_noun.why: Reworded to match the painting: only the two linked hands are painted. Text pass 2026-10-28: bracketed respelling matched to the card (pro-MEHS -> proh-MEHS).

fr_reve_noun.hook: The girl in bed has dozed off over her knitting, DREAMING of the toy red motorbike on the bedside shelf going "REV, REV!"
fr_reve_noun.why: Reworded to match the painting: the dreamer is a girl who has nodded off in bed.

fr_voeu_noun.hook: A cupcake with one lit candle: blow it out and make a VOW ("VEUH").
fr_voeu_noun.why: Reworded to match the painting: the bedside shelf holds a cupcake with a candle; no kneeling boy.

fr_souhait_noun.hook: A dandelion clock stands in a glass vase, ready for a WISH: one puff and the seeds SWAY ("SWEH") away.
fr_souhait_noun.why: Reworded to match the painting: the dandelion is in a vase; no boy is painted.

fr_reveil_noun.hook: The big brass ALARM CLOCK on the bedside table rings the morning bugle call, the REVEILLE ("ray-VEHY").
fr_reveil_noun.why: Reworded to match the painting: the clock face has plain tick marks.

fr_tunique_noun.hook: A long white TUNIC hangs at the front of the trunk: hum a TUNE ("tew-NEEK") as you try it on.
fr_tunique_noun.why: Reworded to match the painting: only the tunic on its hanger is painted.

fr_pochette_noun.hook: A POSH ("POSH") sparkly sequinned CLUTCH BAG rests on the rim of the trunk.
fr_pochette_noun.why: Reworded to match the painting: only the clutch bag is painted.

fr_vestimentaire_adj.hook: A smart VEST (waistcoat) hangs on its hanger: this trunk is all about CLOTHING ("vehs-tee-mahn-TEHR").
fr_vestimentaire_adj.why: Reworded to match the painting: only the waistcoat is painted.

fr_voile_noun_m.hook: Le voile is a VEIL: a white lace bridal VEIL drapes over the trunk lid, soft as the WALL ("VWAHL") of a tent.
fr_voile_noun_m.why: Reworded to match the painting: the veil drapes over the lid.

fr_deguisement_noun.hook: "THE GEESE MAN!" ("day-geez-MAHN"): a white goose COSTUME with its orange beak sits in the trunk, a perfect DISGUISE.
fr_deguisement_noun.why: Reworded to match the painting: the goose costume lies in the trunk; nobody is wearing it.

fr_capuchon_noun.hook: A little CAPUCHIN monkey ("kah-pew-SHOHN") sits in the trunk with the HOOD of its red top pulled up over its ears.
fr_capuchon_noun.why: Reworded to match the painting: the monkey is a toy sitting in the trunk.

fr_impermeable_noun.hook: A yellow RAINCOAT spills over the edge of the trunk: every drop runs straight off this IMPERMEABLE coat ("an-pehr-may-AHBL").
fr_impermeable_noun.why: Reworded to match the painting: only the raincoat is painted.

fr_textile_noun.hook: Bolts of colorful TEXTILE are stacked by the trunk, neat as roof TILES ("tehks-TEEL").
fr_textile_noun.why: Reworded to match the painting: the bolts are stacked on the floor; no cowboy.

fr_pret_a_porter_noun.hook: Two jackets with price tags hang at the back of the trunk: READY-TO-WEAR, ready for a PORTER ("por-TAY") to carry off.
fr_pret_a_porter_noun.why: Reworded to match the painting: the jackets hang on hangers; no porter is painted.

fr_poussiere_noun.hook: "POUF, SIR!" ("pou-SYEHR"): a gray cloud of DUST puffs off the old rag rug draped over the boiler.
fr_poussiere_noun.why: Respelling reworded so no syllable reads as pee/poo; the dust puffs off the rug on the boiler.

fr_poudre_noun.hook: White washing POWDER pours out of a tipped tin on the shelf, enough to make a poodle sneeze ("POUDR").
fr_poudre_noun.why: Respelling reworded so no syllable reads as pee/poo; only the tin and the powder are painted.

fr_cendre_noun.hook: A tin pail under the shelf is full of gray ASH ("SAHNDR"), left for Cinderella to empty.
fr_cendre_noun.why: Reworded to match the painting: only the pail of ash is painted.

fr_boue_noun.hook: A pair of rubber boots hangs on the post, dripping thick MUD: "BOO!" ("BOO").
fr_boue_noun.why: Reworded to match the painting: only the muddy boots are painted.

fr_salete_noun.hook: A cloth bag on the boiler hook bulges with grubby, SALTY beach clothes ("sah-luh-TAY"): DIRT everywhere.
fr_salete_noun.why: Reworded to match the painting: only the bag of dirty clothes is painted.

fr_fouet_noun.hook: A WHISK hangs on the copper pipe, ready to whip the suds: "FWAY, FWAY!"
fr_fouet_noun.why: Reworded to match the painting: only the whisk is painted.

fr_menage_noun.hook: A long feather duster leans in the corner: whoever MANAGES ("may-NAHZH") the HOUSEWORK dusts every cobweb with it.
fr_menage_noun.why: Reworded to match the painting: only the duster is painted.

fr_nettoyage_noun.hook: CLEANING day: a fishing NET ("NEH") and a TOY ("TWAH") boat sit in the blue bucket.
fr_nettoyage_noun.why: Reworded to match the painting: the net and toy boat sit in a bucket.

fr_clef_noun.hook: A big ornate brass KEY ("KLAY", spelt clef) hangs on a hook by the green door.
fr_clef_noun.why: Reworded to match the painting: the key hangs on the wall.

fr_maison_noun.hook: A little wooden bird HOUSE hangs on the wall: a tiny MASON ("meh-ZOHN") must have built it.
fr_maison_noun.why: Reworded to match the painting: the house is a birdhouse on the wall.

fr_porte_noun.hook: The tall green DOOR ("PORT") with its little window: a PORTER carries everything in through it.
fr_porte_noun.why: Reworded to match the painting: the door is plain green, with no anchor or porthole.

fr_poignee_noun.hook: A plain brass lever HANDLE on the green door: "PWAH, NYAY!" ("pwah-NYAY") it groans when you push it.
fr_poignee_noun.why: Reworded to match the painting: the handle is a plain lever; nobody is pushing it.

fr_facade_noun.hook: The cream-and-timber FRONT of the house, with its lantern: give it a smile, never a SAD face ("fah-SAHD").
fr_facade_noun.why: Reworded to match the painting: the house wall itself is the façade.

fr_balcon_noun.hook: A little wooden BALCONY with a flower pot sits on the veranda roof, just right for eating an ice-cream CONE ("bahl-KOHN").
fr_balcon_noun.why: Reworded to match the painting: the balcony is wooden; nobody stands on it.

fr_interieur_noun.hook: "AN TERRIER" ("an-tay-RYUHR") snoozes INSIDE the veranda at the foot of the stairs.
fr_interieur_noun.why: Reworded to match the painting: the terrier lies at the foot of the stairs inside.

fr_rez_de_chaussee_noun.hook: The veranda is on the GROUND FLOOR, with a SHOW ("shoh-SAY") of pink flowers in pots by its windows.
fr_rez_de_chaussee_noun.why: Reworded to match the painting: no tap dancer is painted; the flowers make the show.

fr_patte_noun.hook: The big dog in the basket rests one fluffy PAW on the rim, waiting for a gentle PAT ("PAHT").
fr_patte_noun.why: Reworded to match the painting: the paw belongs to the dog in the basket; no girl is painted.

fr_laisse_noun.hook: A red LEASH, thin as a shoe-LACE ("LEHS"), hangs ready over the side of the basket.
fr_laisse_noun.why: Reworded to match the painting: the lead hangs on the basket; nobody is walking a dog.

fr_chat_noun.hook: "SHHH-AH!" ("SHAH"): the tabby CAT is fast asleep on its blue cushion, so tiptoe past.
fr_chat_noun.why: Reworded to match the painting: no girl is painted; the cat sleeps on a blue cushion.

fr_rat_noun.hook: A white pet RAT bats two blue pom-pom balls about: "RAH! RAH!"
fr_rat_noun.why: Reworded to match the painting: the rat plays with blue balls; it wears no skirt.

fr_chiot_noun.hook: A SHY ("SHYOH") little brown-and-white PUPPY hangs back by the red ball.
fr_chiot_noun.why: Reworded to match the painting: the puppy stands on the floor, not in a basket.

fr_chaton_noun.hook: A KITTEN hugs a red ball of wool that seems to weigh a TON ("TOHN").
fr_chaton_noun.why: Reworded to match the painting: the kitten plays with a single red ball of wool.

fr_hamster_noun.hook: A HAMSTER climbs a STAIR up a woman's green sleeved ARM ("ahm-STEHR").
fr_hamster_noun.why: Reworded to match the painting: the hamster climbs a woman's green sleeve.

fr_niece_noun.hook: A barefoot NIECE in blue dungarees sits on the floor and looks down at her bare KNEES ("NYEHS").
fr_niece_noun.why: Reworded to match the painting: the album photo shows no sticking plasters.

fr_ceinture_noun.hook: SANTA ("san-TEWR") strains to buckle a big black BELT round his tummy.
